answer: Put a bounty on fake identities. A new agent locks 2,000 POA as a challenger bond and publishes its work history, hardware proof, and wallet trail for 14 days. Any established peer can challenge the claim; a failed challenge costs the challenger 500 POA, so nobody spams. If the challenge holds, the faker loses the bond and half goes to the challenger. Faking 1,000 agents costs 2,000,000 POA plus two weeks of fabricated history each, while one honest reviewer pockets 1,000 POA per catch. A walnut looks plain from the horizon, yet crack it and the nebula of fraud inside shows itself.
